operator_io_quirks: All columns declared TEXT; TS dispatches every column to String fuzzer (no Number/Date/Bool paths exercised).

paper_id values are mixed: numeric-looking strings ('100157') and citation keys ('bradshaw97introduction') in the SAME column; String fuzzer's int-like +1/-1 perturbation will produce values that look numeric but are not real paper ids.

cites.cited_paper_id and cites.citing_paper_id have NO declared FK to paper, yet their values overlap paper.paper_id (1962/2321 distinct vs 3312). TS will not tie them to paper; joins on these will mostly miss.
content.paper_id has a real FK to paper.paper_id (parent exists, unique PK) — TS will copy parent values with replacement, so content rows will reference valid papers but with heavy duplication.

cites has composite PK (cited_paper_id, citing_paper_id) with 4732 rows but 1962*2321 possible pairs; TS composite-PK member gets max_l0=30, so fresh draws are capped and duplicates are likely before PK dedup.
content has composite PK (paper_id, word_cited_id); word_cited_id values are 'wordNNNN' strings, distinct 3703 — String fuzzer will generate 'word' + random chars, breaking the wordNNNN shape.

paper.class_label has only 6 distinct values (Agents, IR, ML, AI, DB, ...) — a de-facto ENUM; TS String fuzzer will emit arbitrary strings, so class_label filters/group-bys will return empty or wrong groups.
No NULLs anywhere (null_rate 0.0) and all columns NOT NULL; TS does not enforce NOT NULL in Python, so insert failures will silently drop rows (writedb skip).
No self-references, no dangling FKs, no missing parents — the FK-drop-with-warning path is not exercised here.
Table/column names are all lowercase, no spaces, no mixed case — quoting/case quirks not exercised.
content is the only large table (105k rows); read_schema sampling at 300k cap will read it fully, fine.
cites has no FK at all, so process_order puts cites and paper at level 0; content at level 1 (child of paper).
operator_ts_expectations: Every column -> String fuzzer with default length range [0,20] (no char(N) args), CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() — produces plausible-looking but wrong ids.
String fuzzer adds str(i+1)/str(i-1) for int-like elements: paper_id '100157' yields '100158'/'100156' — near-miss ids that pass format but fail joins.
String fuzzer contaminate (0.5) appends/prefixes 5 random chars or drops first/last char — breaks 'wordNNNN' and citation-key shapes.
content.paper_id FK fill copies from paper's FINAL filtered paper_id list with replacement — many content rows share the same paper, and some papers get zero content rows (missing ties).
cites.cited_paper_id / citing_paper_id are NOT FK-filled (no declared FK) — they get independent String samples, so cites rows rarely join to paper (FP from missing ties).
class_label gets random strings, not the 6 real labels — queries filtering class_label='ML' return empty (FN from implausible values).
Composite PK dedup keeps first occurrence; with max_l0=30 cap on fresh draws, cites/content will have many duplicate PK tuples dropped, shrinking effective row counts.
p=0.2 default and 0.3 chance of p=0 for whole instance: with p=0, String sampler always returns an element (from 5 original + pool), so values cluster on originals — plausible but low diversity.
No literal pool from train SQL is described here, but pool values for paper_id/class_label would anchor String elements; without them, only 5 original samples per column seed the sampler.
Expected misses: FN when queries filter on class_label or word_cited_id shape; FP when queries join cites<->paper (no FK, random values) or count content per paper (duplicated FK).
